sections.section_title: 1. Clinical Presentation and Early Postoperative Course
sections.description: This chapter outlines the patient’s baseline status, procedural details, and the timeline of laboratory and clinical changes that prompted further investigation. It highlights how early postoperative thrombocytopenia coupled with neurologic decline deviated from expected postoperative patterns.
subtopics: Baseline demographics and cardiovascular comorbidities
Pre‑operative anticoagulation and diagnostic catheterisation
Surgical procedure and peri‑operative heparin exposure (CPB and catheterisation)
Post‑operative anticoagulation strategy (LMWH, fondaparinux)
Platelet count trajectory from POD1 to POD6
Development of delirium and subsequent imaging findings (parietal infarct)
Differential emergence of thrombocytopenia in the early postoperative period

sections.description: This section delves into the diagnostic work‑up that ruled out common causes of post‑cardiac‑surgery thrombocytopenia and focused the diagnostic algorithm on heparin‑induced thrombocytopenia (HIT), including the use of serological assays and functional platelet‑activation tests.
subtopics: Peripheral smear assessment (absence of schistocytes, platelet clumps)
Coagulation profile (PT, aPTT, fibrinogen, D‑dimer) and interpretation in early post‑op phase
Serum biochemistry (hemoglobin, reticulocyte count, haptoglobin, B12) to exclude hemolysis and marrow suppression
PF4/polyanion ELISA for HIT antibody screening
Serotonin‑release assay (SRA) – normal vs heparin‑dependent vs heparin‑independent profiles
Interpretation of absent activation at high UFH concentrations
Role of FcγRIIa blocking antibody (IV.3) to distinguish antibody mechanisms

sections.section_title: 3. Diagnostic Reasoning: From Classical HIT to Autoimmune HIT
sections.description: This chapter explains the step‑by‑step clinical reasoning that led from a preliminary HIT diagnosis to the identification of autoimmune HIT (aHIT). It emphasizes the importance of early onset, pre‑operative heparin exposure, and atypical laboratory patterns.
subtopics: Temporal relationship between heparin exposure and platelet count fall
Exclusion of alternative etiologies (infection, thrombosis, drug‑induced thrombocytopenia)
Criteria for aHIT: early onset, heparin‑independent platelet activation
Significance of strong serotonin release at 0 U/mL UFH
Partial inhibition by IV.3 antibody – implications for antibody avidity and FcR engagement
Evolution of SRA profile over time (persistent heparin‑independent activity to later heparin‑dependent pattern)
Clinical relevance of patient‑specific antibody characteristics

sections.section_title: 4. Management Strategy for Severe Autoimmune HIT
sections.description: This section discusses the therapeutic approach tailored to this patient’s severe aHIT, including anticoagulant selection, adjunctive high‑dose IVIG, monitoring of coagulation markers, and transition to long‑term oral anticoagulation.
subtopics: Rationale for discontinuing fondaparinux and starting argatroban
Monitoring via aPTT, fibrinogen, D‑dimer, and peripheral smear for consumptive coagulopathy
High‑dose intravenous Ig protocol and expected platelet response
Assessment of anticoagulation efficacy (fibrinogen decline, D‑dimer trend, schistocyte appearance)
Switch to fondaparinux – indications, dosing, antithrombin supplementation
Criteria for transition back to apixaban and timing of resumption
Long‑term anticoagulation considerations in aHIT

sections.description: This chapter summarizes the patient’s recovery trajectory, the evolution of laboratory findings, and the broader clinical implications for diagnosing and treating aHIT in the peri‑operative setting.
subtopics: Platelet count recovery timeline and neuro‑functional outcomes
Serial SRA results – progression from heparin‑independent to heparin‑dependent activity
Persistently high SRA reactivity despite clinical remission – implications for monitoring
Key take‑aways: early postoperative HIT, aHIT serology, partial IV.3 inhibition
Recommendations for clinicians encountering early thrombocytopenia post‑cardiac surgery
Implications for peri‑operative heparin vigilance and pre‑op anticoagulation management
Future directions: need for assays to detect atypical aHIT antibodies and guide therapy
